analysis: Examined the supplied changes: an additive optional ChipModelEarning type and by_chip / by_chip_window fields in desktop-app/src/shared/contracts.ts (lines 193-206), two new test files and a test fixture, and a doc update in docs/developer/desktop-app.md (lines 421-430). The changes are TypeScript type definitions, test fixtures and documentation. They add no runtime code to the provider, coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), attestation (TB-009, TB-011), key custody (A-002, A-003), prefix-cache (T-041), fan helper, hold socket or sandbox installer paths. They handle no prompts, keys, tokens or authorization. The new per-chip data is public network aggregate earnings, relayed as strings that tests treat as untrusted. The tests show that malformed input (negative, non-integer, wrong type, zero machines, stale as_of) falls back to network totals. This is the correct fail-safe posture. It affects only which models the UI recommends. It does not change the autopilot action authority or any serving permission. Remaining limits: the implementation of recommendations.ts (chipEarnings, chipRanking, recommendedModels) is not in the supplied units, so parsing of untrusted runtime/coordinator data (e.g. BigInt conversion of unbounded strings, rendering) is not verified. This is an integration question for whichever batch contains that file. Nothing in these units contradicts the threat model or needs a model update.
